report:
**Conclusion:** High-quality clinical evidence confirms that ivermectin does **not** lower the risk of death or severe illness from COVID-19. 

Early interest in ivermectin stemmed from small observational reports and low-quality or subsequently retracted studies. However, robust clinical research demonstrates no benefit:

* **Large Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs):**
  * **TOGETHER Trial:** In a double-blind trial of 1,358 symptomatic outpatients, early treatment with ivermectin failed to reduce hospitalizations or mortality compared to placebo (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869).
  * **ACTIV-6 Trial:** Testing higher-dose ivermectin (600 μg/kg daily for 6 days) among outpatients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 showed no improvement in recovery time or prevention of severe outcomes (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2801827).
  * **I-TECH Trial:** A randomized trial in high-risk COVID-19 patients found that ivermectin did not significantly reduce progression to severe disease or all-cause mortality (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamainternalmedicine/fullarticle/2789362).

* **Systematic Reviews:** Rigorous meta-analyses assessing published RCTs found that when methodologically flawed or biased trials are excluded, ivermectin shows no statistically significant reduction in all-cause mortality, length of stay, or viral load (https://academic.oup.com/cid/article/74/6/1022/6310839).

Based on these high-quality trial data, major health authorities and clinical guidelines recommend against using ivermectin to treat COVID-19.
